title: Telegram topic history restore and wide tables

origin.quote:
1. Как только я вышел из keryx shell топик убился, когда я запустил с продолжением keryx shell подхватил сессию, но топик создался новый и пустой. Это правильно, но нудна команда восстановить историю, и по ней присылать в топик 10 последних сообщений(и мои и агента)
2 смотри скриншоты. 1 это что пришло, 2 это как в keryx shell

[verify: exec]" -> "Restored messages arrive oldest first, each as its own message carrying a role label (the operator and the agent differ by text, not only by colour); a fixture with 25 turns posts exactly turns 16 to 25, in that order, and no timestamps are shown (D1). [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" (attach a runnable verification command to every history criterion; no criterion was confirmed yet)

AC10: "The restored messages are separate posts (10 by default, no digest) sent through the outbound queue with pacing: the queue spaces them, a 429 pauses it and the history resumes where it stopped, and no message is posted twice after the pause. [verify: exec]" -> "The restored messages are separate posts (10 by default, no digest) sent through the outbound queue; the bridge spaces the posts by a pace (the queue itself does no pacing), a 429 pauses the queue and the history resumes where it stopped, and no message is posted twice after the pause. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" (the queue is a plain FIFO with no pacing; the implemented pacing lives in the bridge, so the criterion now says so)

AC11: "With an empty session, or one with no qualifying messages, nothing is posted automatically and `/history` answers with one short line that the history is empty, not with silence and not with an error. [verify: exec]" -> "With an empty session, or one with no qualifying messages, nothing is posted automatically and /history answers with one short line that the history is empty, not with silence and not with an error. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" (attach a runnable verification command to every history criterion; no criterion was confirmed yet)

AC12: "A reconnect, a heartbeat, a bridge restart in the same topic, or an at-least-once outbound retry does not repost the history; a second `/history` repeats it on purpose. The automatic restore is remembered by a marker kept per topic in session state, and a test restarts the bridge three times and counts one automatic restore. [verify: exec]" -> "A reconnect, a heartbeat, a bridge restart that re-registers the same session in the same topic (reused: true), or an at-least-once outbound retry does not repost the history; a second /history repeats it on purpose. No persistent marker is kept: the automatic restore happens only on the registration of this enable() that created the topic, and only the first registration counts, so a test that reconnects the client and re-enables with a kept topic counts one automatic restore. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" (the implementation takes reused from the first registration only, so no per-topic marker is needed; the criterion described a marker that does not exist)

AC1: "A probe sends the same wide 3-column table to the operator's keryx-shell topic in three forms (A: the current `table` block, B: rich `markdown` after helyx's separator rewrite, C: HTML `<pre>` aligned table) and records, for each, whether it is wide, whether it scrolls sideways, and its rendered height; only the three test tables are sent, with no secrets, and the message ids are recorded in the flow's spike notes (`.metaproject/flows/399-2026-10-03-topic-history-and-wide-tables/spike.md`) together with the chosen variant and why. [verify: judged]" -> "A probe sends the same wide table to the operator keryx-shell topic in three forms (A: the current table block, B: rich markdown sent as is, C: HTML pre aligned table) and records the message ids and, for each form, whether Telegram accepted it, and whether it is wide, scrolls sideways and how tall it renders; only the three test tables are sent, with no secrets, and the ids go to the flow spike notes (.metaproject/flows/399-2026-10-03-topic-history-and-wide-tables/spike.md) together with the chosen variant and why. [verify: judged]" (the probe table has 6 columns to be wide enough to overflow, and helyx separator rewrite is not available to this repository, so B is rich markdown sent as is)

AC8: "Every restored message goes through the same redaction as a live reply (composeReply) and is cut at the per-item cap (D2) with an ellipsis marker; a session fixture holding a token-shaped string and a 40,000-character turn yields a topic payload with the token redacted and the turn cut. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" -> "Every restored message goes through the same redaction as a live reply (composeReply) and is cut at the per-item cap (D2) with an ellipsis marker; a turn whose text has a bot-token shape or a bare high-entropy token is not posted and is replaced by a placeholder (a restore-time guard on top of the shared redactor, which can miss them); a session fixture holding a token-shaped string and a 40,000-character turn yields a topic payload with no token and the long turn cut. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" (Independent review of PR 870: the shared redactor misses a pasted bot token and a bare base64url token, so a guard replaces such a turn)

AC12: "A reconnect, a heartbeat, a bridge restart that re-registers the same session in the same topic (reused: true), or an at-least-once outbound retry does not repost the history; a second /history repeats it on purpose. No persistent marker is kept: the automatic restore happens only on the registration of this enable() that created the topic, and only the first registration counts, so a test that reconnects the client and re-enables with a kept topic counts one automatic restore. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" -> "A reconnect, a heartbeat, a bridge restart that re-registers the same session in the same topic (reused: true), or an at-least-once outbound retry does not repost the history; a second /history repeats it on purpose. Turning remote control off and on again in the same process makes a new topic and restores nothing into it (use /history). No persistent marker is kept: the automatic restore happens only on the first enable() of the process and only on the first registration of that enable() (the one that created the topic), so a test that reconnects the client and one that turns it off and on each count one automatic restore at most. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/topic-history.test.ts`]" (Independent review of PR 870: off/on reposted, contradicting the docs; the behaviour and the criterion now say nothing is posted)

AC2: "The chosen table variant is built by a pure function whose output for a fixed corpus of tables (2 to 20 columns, empty cells, cells with `|`, Cyrillic, emoji, a 300-character cell) is pinned by a test; a table with more than 20 columns degrades to the HTML or plain form instead of failing. Short and 2-column tables follow D5. [verify: exec]" -> "The table path is unchanged by this flow (the operator chose variant A, the native `table` block, in the probe): a test pins the output of `renderRichMessage` for a fixed corpus of tables (2 to 20 columns, empty cells, cells with `|`, Cyrillic, emoji, a 300-character cell) as typed blocks with every cell whole (no cell is shortened anywhere on the table path); a table with more than 20 columns is not recognised as a table and goes out as HTML. Short and 2-column tables follow D5. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/format-table-pins.test.ts`]" (Operator chose variant A (today's native table block): no new builder, the existing behaviour is pinned instead)

AC3: "Every invariant flow 395 already holds for rich replies still holds for the new table path: escaping, block balance, model text never reaches a parser it was not meant for (a cell containing Markdown or block syntax stays a cell), and the property corpus passes unchanged. [verify: exec]" -> "Every invariant flow 395 already holds for rich replies is unchanged and pinned by tests: escaping, block balance, model text never reaches a parser it was not meant for (a cell containing Markdown or block syntax stays a cell), and the property corpus passes unchanged. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/format-property.test.ts src/remote/format-rich.test.ts src/remote/format-table-pins.test.ts`]" (Operator chose variant A: nothing new reaches a parser, the invariants are pinned, not extended)

AC4: "The HTML fallback and the plain-text fallback of a table are byte-for-byte what they are before this flow (golden files compared); a send refused by Telegram still falls back in the same order. [verify: exec]" -> "The HTML fallback and the plain-text fallback of a table are unchanged and pinned by literal expected strings (the aligned layout, the stacked layout for a row over the cost limit), and the fall from rich to HTML to plain keeps its order when Telegram refuses a send. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/format-table-pins.test.ts src/remote/outbound-rich.test.ts`]" (Operator chose variant A: the fallbacks are what they were, pinned by tests instead of golden files of a new variant)

AC5: "A reply with a table too large for one message is split at row boundaries, never inside a row, and each part repeats the header row; the parts are sent in order and none exceeds 4096 characters (ordinary) or the rich-message limits (32768 characters, 500 blocks). [verify: exec]" -> "A reply with a table too large for one message is split at row boundaries, never inside a row, and each part repeats the header row; the parts are sent in order; none exceeds 4096 rendered characters (ordinary) and none exceeds the rich-message limits (32768 characters, 500 blocks, where a table row is a block), so a part of a tall table still goes out as a native table instead of falling to HTML. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/format-table-pins.test.ts src/remote/format-table.test.ts`]" (Pinning AC5 showed that the splitter charged rendered characters only: a table of more than 500 rows fitted one 4096-character part and was refused by the rich limit, so it lost its native table)

AC18: "README, `docs/docs/guides/drive-keryx-remotely.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` describe the new table layout, with a version bump, and `mkdocs build --strict` passes; live acceptance by the operator: ask the agent for a wide table and confirm it reads like helyx's, with horizontal scroll when it does not fit. [verify: judged]" -> "README, `docs/docs/guides/drive-keryx-remotely.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` describe how a table reaches Telegram (the native wide table with horizontal scroll, no cell shortening, the 20-column cap, the HTML and plain fallbacks, the row cap per part), with a version bump, and `mkdocs build --strict` passes; live acceptance by the operator: ask the agent for a wide table and confirm it reads like helyx, with horizontal scroll when it does not fit. [verify: judged]" (Operator chose variant A: there is no new table layout to describe, only the behaviour that is now pinned)

AC5: "A reply with a table too large for one message is split at row boundaries, never inside a row, and each part repeats the header row; the parts are sent in order; none exceeds 4096 rendered characters (ordinary) and none exceeds the rich-message limits (32768 characters, 500 blocks, where a table row is a block), so a part of a tall table still goes out as a native table instead of falling to HTML. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/format-table-pins.test.ts src/remote/format-table.test.ts`]" -> "A reply with a table too large for one message is split at row boundaries, never inside a row (except a single cell larger than a whole message), and each part repeats the header row; the parts are sent in order; none exceeds 4096 rendered characters (ordinary) and a part that holds a table stays within the rich-message limits (32768 characters, 500 blocks counted for the whole part: a table row, a paragraph, a list item each cost blocks), so a part of a tall table, or of a table with text around it, still goes out as a native table instead of falling to HTML; a row too large to share a message with the header is written as stacked header: value lines. [verify: exec `bun test src/remote/format-table-pins.test.ts src/remote/format-table.test.ts`]" (#871 review: the row cap counted only table rows and 'never inside a row' was false for a row over a message; the criterion now states the whole-part block budget and the defined behaviour for an oversized row)
